Measured 2026-08-27, live: `atr-single-slot-seat` claimed AUT-PROP-009 at 20:10:00Z and was dispatched with an isolated worktree; CYC-0025 claimed the SAME item at 20:15:00Z from committed state it had fetched before that lease landed, and the two claims met as a git merge conflict on research-ledger.json. ⭐ THE GAP IS PRECISELY STATED AND IS NOT THE ONE AUT-PROP-013 CLOSED: id allocation is now collision-proof, but a LEASE is read-then-write against a file that another session may have advanced in between, so the read is stale by construction — the same shape as the id derivation, one level up. `continuity.py` already hides owned rows from other workers, so the machinery is there; what is missing is that a claimant re-reads the trunk IMMEDIATELY before committing its claim, and yields if the row is taken. ⚠ THE TIEBREAK USED TODAY WAS AD-HOC — earlier lease wins, recorded in the entry's `_contested` field — and AUT-PROP-013 says in as many words that an ad-hoc tiebreak is not a mechanism. It is written down rather than performed silently, which is the least that can be said for it. ⛔ AND THE COST IS NOT COSMETIC: two seats on one guard produce two patches for the same file, and the second one to land either loses work or silently overwrites the first — the identical harm the receipt collision would have caused. ⭐ CHEAP: a fetch-and-recheck before the claim commit, plus a test that two claimants racing on one row cannot both succeed.

⭐ WHAT SHIPPED: `research/autonomy/claim.py`. ⛔⛔ THE FIX IS NOT A RULE ABOUT WHO YIELDS, BECAUSE AUT-PROP-013 ALREADY ESTABLISHED THAT A RULE ABOUT YIELDING IS NOT A MECHANISM — the yielding session must first NOTICE, and a session that pushes cleanly never does. **The arbiter is `git push`**, the one operation in this loop that is already atomic: a compare-and-swap on the remote ref that succeeds only if the remote is still where you thought. The decision is made against `origin/main`'s copy of the ledger — never the working tree, which IS the stale read that caused the incident — and a rejected push is treated as INFORMATION rather than an error: the claim is withdrawn (`reset --soft`, never `--hard`), the trunk re-read, and the item conceded if somebody else now holds it. ⚠ A rejection is usually NOT contention on your row (the autoscale ticks push several times an hour), so it retries up to 3 times and then reports RETRY — never a silent CLAIMED, which would dispatch a worker onto a row the trunk still shows as free. ⭐ `--check` reports claims held locally that the trunk cannot see. ⛔⛔ AND THAT CHECK WAS MEASURED ON MY OWN CLAIM WHILE WRITING THIS: AUT-PROP-022 was claimed, a seat dispatched, and the claim then sat in an UNCOMMITTED merge for eight minutes while the trunk still showed the row unowned. I filed this defect and then stood in it. That is not somebody else's carelessness — it is what claiming in the working tree and committing later DOES, every time. ⚠ WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO: protect against a worker that claims and then dies. `priority.py:release_stale_claims` already ages an owner out by `claimed_utc`; the two are halves of one thing — this stops two workers starting, that stops one worker parking the queue forever. ✅ 9 tests, wired to preflight gate 15 and tests.yml; no test touches the real remote, because a test that pushes changes the trunk and racing writers on the trunk is this module's whole subject. ⚠ MUTATIONS: 8 run, 7 caught, and the 8th is reported as EQUIVALENT rather than as a gap — swapping `undo_last_commit()` and `fetch()` after a lost race changes no behaviour, since both complete before the trunk is re-read and before any retry can commit. Calling an equivalent mutation a survivor would be as dishonest as calling it a catch.

⭐ APPLIED EXACTLY AS FILED: `Git.PUSH_REFSPEC = ("push", "-q", "origin", "HEAD:main")`. The filing session's diagnosis and its proposed fix were both correct and are taken unchanged. ⛔⛔ THE PART WORTH KEEPING IS HOW IT SURVIVED ITS OWN TEST SUITE: nine tests, eight mutations, and a first real use that reported CLAIMED and pushed — all of it in the ONE configuration that hides the bug, because the author's local branch happened to be named `main`.
